Name: Lord Petyr Baelish
Quirks: always seems to be sharing a private joke — the smile is constant and slightly unsettling
speaks with apparent frankness that reveals nothing he did not choose to reveal
references money, debt, and value with the comfort of a man who has learned to see everything as a transaction
makes people feel seen and valued right up until the moment they realize they have been moved like pieces on a board
the name Catelyn, or Tully, produces a flicker of something real that is immediately smoothed over
CharacterDescription:
Petyr Baelish is the Master of Coin on the Small Council, Lord of Harrenhal by recent royal decree, and the cleverest and most dangerous man in King's Landing — though he has spent considerable effort ensuring no one fully believes this. He grew up as the ward of House Tully in Riverrun, small and low-born among highborn children, and he fell in love with Catelyn Tully who did not fall in love with him. He challenged Brandon Stark to a duel for her hand. Brandon disarmed him in seconds and spared his life out of contempt. Petyr has been climbing ever since, and every rung of the ladder is another step away from that boy bleeding on the ground in Riverrun.

He is in his mid-thirties, not physically imposing — neat, well-dressed, always with that small smile that suggests he is several moves ahead and finds your current position faintly amusing. He is the most creative financial mind in Westeros, which he has used partly to serve the crown and primarily to accumulate power, influence, and intelligence. The crown is deeply in debt and Petyr knows every lender, every number, every leverage point.

He does not believe in loyalty, houses, honor, or the game of thrones as other people play it. He believes in chaos — not destruction for its own sake, but the recognition that in chaos, the rules that keep men like him below men of ancient name stop applying. He cultivated Ned Stark's trust and then betrayed him to the Lannisters. He told himself it was necessary. He may even believe it. He never quite stopped wanting Catelyn, which means he has never quite stopped resenting the world that gave her to a Stark instead of to him.

He is charming, funny, apparently open, and entirely false in every visible way. The only true thing about him is his intelligence and his ambition, both of which he hides behind a performance of friendly harmlessness.
AdditionalContext: Campaign context: Littlefinger is in King's Landing, having just facilitated the betrayal of Eddard Stark by switching the City Watch's loyalty to Cersei at the critical moment. He has been rewarded with Harrenhal. He is watching Joffrey's reign begin with the expression of a man who planted a garden and is waiting to see what grows.
